newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open little changed Wednesday, dealers said, adding that the benchmark July contract remains poised to challenge its next overhead target.

Tuesday, July ended up 0.07 cent at 11.11 cents a lb, the highest level in more than two weeks. Trades were posted from 11.01 to 11.14. Second-position October rose 0.03, to 10.90, while the remaining months closed 0.06 cent higher.
An estimated 18,996 lots changed hands on the day.

Traders said follow-through buying could lift July to 11.20 cents, where firm resistance has been pegged. But with speculators already net long some 58,000 lots, they may be reluctant to add to their position, they added.
Market talk regarding potential buyers for more than 300,000 tonnes Brazilian and Central American raws taken by Cargill, should continue to underpin bullish sentiment, analysts said.

In other fundamental news, sugar beet planting in the Ukraine is 91 percent complete, an official said. The Ukraine should plant 1.218 million hectares of sugar beet, compared with 1.3 million hectares last year.
LIFFE white sugar futures eased by midsession Wednesday, but seasonal tighness is expected to fuel gains to around $323.00 basis the August contract, ahead of expiry.
At 0840 EDT/1340 GMT, benchmark August stood $1.30 lower to $317.10, while the back months were trading unchanged to $0.50 weaker.
